correctness.rationale: For circle Haar probability, the integral is the squared coefficient norm of (a+bz+cz²)³. Among its seven coefficients, only 3a(ac+b²), b(6ac+b²), and 3c(ac+b²) carry interference, and their squared moduli give a single cosine of δ=2arg b−arg a−arg c with coefficient 6AB²C(3A²+2B²+3C²). When ABC>0, both phases are achievable and the minimum integral is positive (also at least (A²+B²+C²)³ by Jensen). If any magnitude vanishes all phases tie. Divide the extrema by (AC)³ and set S=(A²+C²)/(AC)≥2 and T=B²/(AC)>0. The denominator H simplifies to S³+9TS²+(6−18T+9T²)S+18T−12T²+T³. The derivative numerator for 12T(3S+2T)/H in S is −36T[2S³+12ST²+5T³+T(11S²−14)], strictly negative. At S=2 the denominator is (T+2)(T²+4T+10); differentiation gives −24 times T⁴+6T³−40T−60 divided by its square. Descartes' rule and the opposite signs at zero and large positive T give exactly one positive root, with the derivative strictly changing from positive to negative. The maximum is attained exactly at A=C>0 and T=t_*, with δ=0,π respectively for the two extrema. A nontrivial integer rescaling preserves Haar by the power map; translating the spectrum only multiplies by a unit modulus monomial. Taking the sixth root gives the norm contrast, not the sixth moment contrast.
residual_risks: The supplied finite quadrature is corroborative; the derivative sign and complete phase argument give the universal proof. Decimal values are approximations to the exact root and rational functions.

originality.rationale: The strongest same-support results give a maximum divided by coefficient energy or a phase response restricted to unit magnitudes. Neither determines the maximal distortion relative to the minimum at the same unknown magnitudes. The known cubic-convolution mechanism is not the distinct claim; the contribution is the exact global ratio, its balancing and unique amplitude optimum. Arestov's 1980 article could not be compared in full; no absence is inferred from that access gap.
residual_risks: Two exact cited IDs were not resolved; the verified distinct earlier maximum-energy record supplies the relevant mathematical comparison, not an identity of citations.
The Arestov primary article was inaccessible, and a historical equivalent in metric or multiplier terminology cannot be excluded by bounded searches.

value.rationale: This is the exact largest phase distortion of the sixth norm for the shortest analytic progression with a genuine relative-phase interaction at this exponent. It measures a different property from the well-studied maximum norm per coefficient energy and identifies a different optimizing amplitude. The optimizer and constant give a concrete reference for coefficient-multiplier distortion on small spectra rather than a new claim about general majorant theory.
residual_risks: Only an arithmetic progression of three frequencies at moment order six is covered; no general exponent, support or Bergman result is claimed.
